## Full data-quality review — registered "Palmer Penguins" CSV

### What was loaded
344 rows, 3 columns, from the registered fixture source.

### Findings by check

**Schema — significant problem.** The profile reports 5 expected Palmer Penguins columns as missing entirely: `bill_depth_mm`, `bill_length_mm`, `body_mass_g`, `flipper_length_mm`, and `year`. The registry advertises these columns, but none are present in the loaded data. Only `species`, `island`, and `sex` exist, and there are no extra/unexpected columns. This is the dominant finding: **roughly all quantitative content of the canonical dataset is absent.** The file is not a faithful Palmer Penguins table as registered.

**Missingness.** 11 missing cells across 11 rows, all in `sex` (3.2% of rows). `species` and `island` are complete. In the upstream dataset these 11 rows are the well-known rows with unrecorded sex. Notably, the canonical file also has 2 rows with missing `body_mass_g` and 2 with missing `bill_depth_mm` — none of those columns exist here, so **their missingness cannot be observed or assessed at all.**

**Duplicates — severe.** 331 repeated rows after the first occurrence, out of 344. Only 13 rows are distinct. For the real Palmer Penguins dataset, the expected duplicate count is 0 (the 344-row file has no repeated records). A 96.2% duplication rate is inconsistent with the registered dataset. Either the fixture was built by replicating a small template, or it is a different artifact that was registered under this name. **I cannot verify which**, since the tools report counts only and I cannot inspect raw cell text.

**Categories — clean.** Zero unexpected cells in all three categorical columns. All `species`, `island`, and `sex` values fall within known categories with no case, whitespace, or spelling variants. The tool does not expose the observed values themselves, so I can confirm validity but not the actual category distribution (e.g. whether all three species and all three islands are represented, or whether the data is collapsed onto a single label).

**Numeric — not applicable.** No measurement columns were detected, and the numeric check returned an empty column map with 0 invalid cells. This is a **vacuous pass, not a clean bill of health**: there was nothing numeric to test. The policy applied is finite-and-positive with no biological plausibility bounds, but with zero numeric columns in scope, positive/finite behavior of `body_mass_g`, `bill_length_mm`, `bill_depth_mm`, and `flipper_length_mm` remains entirely unverified.

### Limitations
- **The dataset does not match its registration.** The 5 absent measurement columns and the 331 repeated rows both point to a mis-registered or corrupted fixture. Any analysis presented as "Palmer Penguins" from this file would be unsupported.
- **Out-of-range and plausibility checks could not be run** on any measurement, and cannot be run at all until the missing columns are supplied.
- **Tool granularity.** I received counts and per-column tallies, not raw values. I could not inspect cell contents, so I cannot diagnose *why* rows repeat (identical records vs. identical key fields with differing unmeasured attributes), and I cannot confirm category distributions.
- **Numeric checks, where applicable to other data, test only positive finite representations** — never biological plausibility. I make no claim that body mass or bill measurements would be realistic even if present.
- **No scientific validity is certified.** Whether the retained categorical fields are factually accurate for the penguins they purportedly describe is outside what these checks can establish.
- I did not delete, repair, reorder, or otherwise modify any data; the review is strictly read-only.

### Bottom line
Two findings dominate: **5 of 8 registered columns are missing**, and **331 of 344 rows are duplicates**. The `sex` column has 11 missing values, and the three categorical columns are internally valid. The one check that returned "clean" on the numeric side passed vacuously because no numeric columns exist. I would not treat this file as fit for quantitative analysis until the missing measurement columns are restored and the duplication is explained or resolved by the data owner.
